transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Hello, doctor. I'm here because I just don’t feel any interest in the community projects and hobbies that used to mean everything to me. I finally agreed to come in at the urging of my pastor and a close friend who noticed I've completely withdrawn from my normal routine.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest and withdrawing from your usual activities?

These feelings have been hanging over me for a little over two years now, ever since that terrible accident at the crosswalk downtown. It really hasn't let up since that night, and I just feel so tired of carrying this heavy cloud around.
Since that accident, do you find yourself experiencing unwanted memories or nightmares about it, or do you actively try to avoid going near that crosswalk?

Yes, both of those things happen to me. If I hear tires screech or see a truck at a crosswalk, I'm suddenly right back on that corner watching the impact, which makes me feel sick and shaky. I also go completely out of my way to avoid that intersection, and I immediately shut down or change the subject if anyone tries to bring up the accident.
Since the accident, have you also noticed feeling constantly on guard, easily startled, or having a lot of trouble sleeping?

Yes, I definitely feel constantly on guard and jumpy. I find myself watching cars like a hawk, checking the street repeatedly before stepping off the curb, and tensing up at every engine rev or loud noise. Even when I'm just sitting in a café, I have to face the door so I can keep an eye on everything around me.
Since the accident, have you been carrying persistent feelings of guilt or blaming yourself for what happened, or do you find yourself having constant negative thoughts about yourself or the world?

Yes, I carry a terrible amount of guilt. I constantly blame myself, thinking that if I’d just moved the group a little faster or waited for the next light, that boy might still be alive today. I feel like I completely failed them, and I have this heavy mix of guilt and dread sitting in my stomach that I just can't shake.
Aside from the guilt and reminders of the accident, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I feel this heavy dread and a dark cloud sitting over me most of the day, and it doesn't lift even when I'm at church or with my grandchildren. I just feel completely blank inside now, and it's hard to remember what it felt like to actually be happy or at ease.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep, or have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or that life is no longer worth living?

My appetite hasn't really changed, but sleeping is very difficult because the memories just won't quiet down at night. I don't have any active plans to hurt myself, but on those bad nights I sometimes drink too much wine and drive too fast on the back roads, thinking "who cares what happens to me anyway," even though I know deep down that's not how I truly feel.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the full diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) following a traumatic crosswalk accident over two years ago. The patient exhibits persistent intrusive memories (flashbacks triggered by screeching tires), active avoidance of the trauma site and discussions, negative alterations in cognition and mood (survivor's guilt, self-blame, anhedonia, and emotional numbing), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, insomnia, and reckless driving). While depressive symptoms (F32) are present, they are secondary to and better explained by the chronic PTSD.
